primary_topics: BLD (Bukas Loob sa Diyos) teaching on the Feast of Christ the King (November 20, 1994), delivered November 23, 1994 -- the earliest speech in the corpus; CJP not yet a Supreme Court justice

Five leadership qualities of Jesus: (1) clear vision and mission (the Sermon on the Mount as the greatest teaching); (2) courage and conviction (mixing with sinners, tax collectors, Samaritan women; speaking against the powerful); (3) servant-leader by example (washing feet, 'whoever aspires to greatness must serve'); (4) intense prayer and faith (Gethsemane blood-like sweat; teaching the Lord's Prayer); (5) justice and love (Romans 14:17; the judge-daughter parable)

The judge-daughter parable in its earliest form: a judge fines his speeding daughter P500, then removes his robe, goes to the cashier and pays the fine himself -- 'he paid the penalty out of love because the law-breaker was his daughter'; Jesus as the supreme judge who paid humanity's penalty out of love
The governing synthesis: 'Such is the love in Jesus. Such is the Leader in Jesus. Such is the King we celebrate. Such is King Jesus.'
sub_topics: Christ the King paradox: 'contrary to this mighty and glorious portrayal of Him as King and Lord, the gospel presents Jesus as a humble man, accused before Pilate -- a relatively minor official, a Roman procurator'; throne = wooden cross, crown = thorns, scepter = lowly reed, ring = rusty nail; constituents chanted 'Crucify Him'

Leadership quality 1 -- Vision and mission: 'Jesus made it absolutely clear who He was, what His objectives were and how He intended to accomplish them. Jesus incessantly articulated His ideas and visions... His mighty sermon on the mount is the greatest teaching of all time and for all time.'

Leadership quality 2 -- Courage and conviction: 'no freedom of speech, no freedom to dissent. Group conformity was the only measure of truth and virtue. But Jesus did not conform. He mixed with sinners, tax collectors, a Samaritan woman, a prostitute and an adulteress. He did not mince words in identifying His opponents and denouncing their sins.'

Leadership quality 3 -- Servant-leader by example: 'Anyone among you who aspires to greatness must serve the rest; whoever wants to rank first among you must serve the needs of all. The Son of Man has not come to be served but to serve -- to give His life in ransom for the many... He led by example, washing the feet of His apostles.'

Leadership quality 4 -- Prayer and faith: 'In the garden of Gethsemane, Jesus prayed so intensely that his sweat became like drops of blood falling to the ground... He taught His disciples the best prayer of all, the Lord's Prayer.'

Leadership quality 5 -- Justice and love: 'Romans 14:17 says that the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating or drinking, but of justice, peace and the joy that is given by the Holy Spirit.' But Jesus is also compassionate and loving; the judge-daughter parable; 'Justice was served -- and so was love.'

The judge-daughter parable (earliest form): 'There was this young lady-driver brought before a judge for speeding. For speeding you are hereby sentenced to pay a fine of P500. After adjourning the court session, the judge removed his black robe, went straight to the court cashier, pulled out his wallet and paid the 500-peso fine. He paid the penalty out of love because the law-breaker was his daughter. Justice was served -- and so was love.'
Governing synthesis: 'Such is the love in Jesus. Such is the Leader in Jesus. Such is the King we celebrate. Such is King Jesus. All hail King Jesus!'

stances.claim: The judge-daughter parable appears here in its earliest form -- November 23, 1994 -- approximately 15 years before its other appearances in the corpus (SC104 January 2010, SC153 November 1994). This is the originating context: a BLD teaching on Christ the King, where justice and love as inseparable divine attributes are the governing theme. CJP is not yet a Supreme Court justice; the parable is pure theological illustration.
stances.rhetorical_move: judge-daughter-as-theological-illustration: the parable's earliest form as pure Christology before its later transformation into judicial philosophy
stances.confidence: asserted as the originating context of the parable in the corpus

stances.claim: Jesus's five leadership qualities -- vision and mission, courage and conviction, servant-leadership by example, prayer and faith, justice and love -- are the governing theological standard against which CJP measures all human leadership throughout the corpus. The servant-leadership quality (washing feet, 'whoever aspires to greatness must serve') is the direct source of CJP's governing conclusion that 'leading by example is the best, if not the only, way to long-term effective leadership.'
stances.rhetorical_move: Jesus-as-leadership-standard-origin: the five leadership qualities as the theological ur-text from which CJP's secular leadership framework is derived
stances.confidence: asserted as the governing origin text of his leadership philosophy

notable_anecdotes: The earliest judge-daughter parable: '...the judge removed his black robe, went straight to the court cashier, pulled out his wallet and paid the 500-peso fine. He paid the penalty out of love because the law-breaker was his daughter. Justice was served -- and so was love.' -- this November 1994 version is the first appearance in the corpus; the parable is here pure Christology, not yet applied to CJP's judicial experience.

Jesus as the unusual King: 'His throne is a wooden cross, His crown a bouquet of thorns, His scepter a lowly reed, and His ring a rusty nail driven on His palm. His constituents betrayed Him, chanting, Crucify Him, Crucify Him. And yet He is the only King who resurrected from the dead and by such resurrection conquered sin not just in His own time but in all eternity.' -- the most theologically compact paradox description in the corpus.

Gethsemane prayer intensity: 'In the garden of Gethsemane, Jesus prayed so intensely that his sweat became like drops of blood falling to the ground' -- the governing image of prayer-as-suffering as the prerequisite for faith leadership.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered November 23, 1994 at a Bukas Loob sa Diyos (BLD) gathering -- the earliest speech in the corpus, approximately one year before CJP's SC appointment -- this teaching by CJP on the Feast of Christ the King (November 20, 1994) presents five leadership qualities of Jesus. The Christ-the-King paradox: 'His throne is a wooden cross, His crown a bouquet of thorns, His scepter a lowly reed, and His ring a rusty nail driven on His palm. His constituents betrayed Him, chanting, Crucify Him. And yet He is the only King who resurrected from the dead and by such resurrection conquered sin not just in His own time but in all eternity.' The five leadership qualities: (1) Vision and mission -- 'His mighty sermon on the mount is the greatest teaching of all time and for all time'; (2) Courage and conviction -- 'no freedom of speech, no freedom to dissent'; yet Jesus 'mixed with sinners, tax collectors, a Samaritan woman, a prostitute and an adulteress. He did not mince words in identifying His opponents'; (3) Servant-leader by example -- 'whoever aspires to greatness must serve the rest... The Son of Man has not come to be served but to serve -- to give His life in ransom for the many'; washing the apostles' feet; (4) Prayer and faith -- 'In the garden of Gethsemane, Jesus prayed so intensely that his sweat became like drops of blood'; teaching the Lord's Prayer; (5) Justice and love (Romans 14:17) -- the judge-daughter parable in its earliest form: a judge fines his speeding daughter P500, then removes his robe and pays the fine himself ('He paid the penalty out of love because the law-breaker was his daughter. Justice was served -- and so was love') -- Jesus paid humanity's penalty out of love. Close: 'Such is the love in Jesus. Such is the Leader in Jesus. Such is the King we celebrate. Such is King Jesus. All hail King Jesus!'
